{"decision": "APPLY", "workflow_yaml": "name: Test
on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
      - production
  pull_request:
    branches:

jobs:
  test:
    name: Run tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Clone repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v3

      - name: Set up node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v3
        with:
          node-version: lts/*

      - name: Cache node modules
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.npm
            node_modules
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-node-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-node-

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --legacy-peer-deps

      - name: Run tests
        run: npm run test", "rationale": "The repository is a Node.js project with a committed package-lock.json, and the workflow installs dependencies on every run without caching. The retrieved experiment batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-1ac2203839ed8c07-r2 (P-LIT-CONFIG-REUSE) measured adding an actions/cache step for node_modules keyed on package-lock.json before install, preserving all original steps and achieving 4.76% elapsed savings with identical success conclusions. Applying the same minimal change here reuses dependency downloads across runs while keeping checkout, setup, install, and test steps unchanged, so build and test coverage is preserved. No permissions, secrets, deployment, or new network access is introduced.", "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-1ac2203839ed8c07-r2"]}
